name: watson-yellott-2012-unified
citation: Watson AB, Yellott JI. A unified formula for light-adapted pupil size. J Vis 12(10):12, 1-16, 2012.
equation: F = L·a·M(e); D_SD = maxMm − rangeMm·(F/fluxScale)^exponent / ((F/fluxScale)^exponent + halfConstant); D_U = D_SD + (y − referenceYears)·(slopeIntercept + slopePerMm·D_SD), with L in cd/m², a in deg², y in years, D in mm
note: The paper was unreachable from the cloud session (2026-10-28). Each block names its source; set verified: true after checking every constant against the paper's equations.

stanleyDavies.source: Search-engine excerpts quoting the Stanley & Davies base function as adopted by Watson & Yellott (e.g. arXiv 2412.00831 Eq. 15) and luxpy 1.12.5 get_pupil_diameter_watson2012; they agree.

age.source: Reference age 28.58 y and the 20–83 y validity range confirmed by search excerpts of the paper. The slope constants are from luxpy 1.12.5 get_pupil_diameter_watson2012 (a secondary, open-source implementation); luxpy's simplified closed form agrees with them to 2e-5 mm. Ages outside the domain are clamped (the paper's appendix extension below 20 y is not used).

monocular.source: luxpy 1.12.5 get_pupil_diameter_watson2012 (M(e) = 0.1 for one eye, 1 for two); not confirmed against the paper.

defaults.note: Viewer defaults, assumptions: binocular viewing of a 60° × 60° adapting field (a room-sized scene).
